# Asteroids ROM Development Guide (Nothing Phone 3a)

Comprehensive engineering runbook and strict development constraints for Android ROM development on **Nothing Phone (3a)** (codename: `asteroids`, SoC: Qualcomm Snapdragon 7s Gen 3 / SM7635 `volcano`).

Derived from session `a886a868-1b9b-4e07-a3ed-76a9e2b765a3`.

- **No Build Cycles:** The user will not run repeated test or bring-up builds. Work must be build-safe from the start.

## 3. Subsystem Technical Runbooks

### 3.1 Sandboxed Google Play (`gmscompat`) vs `PixelPropsUtils`
- **Rule:** Never run `gmscompat` and `PixelPropsUtils` spoofing concurrently in the same process.
- In `frameworks/base`: `PixelPropsUtils` must yield when `GmsCompat` is enabled:
  ```java
  if (GmsCompat.isEnabled()) {
      return;
  }
  ```
- **Integrity & Attestation:**
  - Clean SELinux policies (`sepolicy`).
  - No boot attestation leaks, clean build dates, eliminate all root detection vectors.
- See detailed guide: [references/gmscompat-pixelprops.md](./references/gmscompat-pixelprops.md)

### 3.2 UI/UX, SystemUI & Launcher3
- **Quick Settings (QS) & Media:**
  - High customizability: portrait/landscape resizable sliders, custom tile dimensions and padding.
  - Clean code without bloated imports; maintain 120Hz smooth rendering.
- **Dynamic Island / Live Activities:**
  - Compact, expanded, and dual-activity views with settings toggle.
  - Check screen curvature and avoid left-edge clipping on Nothing Phone (3a) panel.
- **Launcher3 & Launcher3Feed:**
  - Integrated with Glanceable Hub (`GlanceOverlay`, `GlanceWidgetFrame`, `GlanceWidgetPickerActivity`).
  - Dark-shaded opaque background mode.
  - Align widget picker dimensions and resize handle visuals against Glanceable Hub standards.
- See detailed guide: [references/ui-ux-systemui.md](./references/ui-ux-systemui.md)

### 3.3 Device Tree & Hardware HAL Auditing (`asteroids`)
- **Reference Tree:** Fairphone 6 (FP6, `lineage-24.0`, SM7635 / volcano).
- **SurfaceFlinger:** Keep cpuset pinned to cores 4-7; keep `predict_hwc_composition_strategy=1`.
- **Vibrator HAL (`hardware/nothing`):**
  - Uses `rt6010` richtap driver.
  - Seed `f0` resonant frequency once on init; do NOT send `RICHTAP_SET_FREQ` on every tap (triggers `KERN_ERR`).
  - Cancel in-flight `compose()` worker threads on `on()` and `perform()`.
- **Audio / Bluetooth:**
  - Apply `LHDCv5` property init guard (`persist.vendor.bt.a2dp.lhdc_v5`).
  - Remove dead legacy audio XML configs and unread effect configs.
- **Camera:**
  - Known issue: OIS calibration symlink `/data/vendor/camera/ois_gyro_offset` permission / DAC 0600.
- **Kernel:**
  - ACK 6.6 with KSU-Next and SUSFS integration. Keep test branch clean.
- See detailed guide: [references/device-tree-audit.md](./references/device-tree-audit.md)

# Device Tree & Hardware HAL Auditing (Nothing Phone 3a / asteroids)

## 1. Hardware Specifications & Reference
- **Codename:** `asteroids` (Nothing Phone (3a))
- **Platform / SoC:** Qualcomm Snapdragon 7s Gen 3 (SM7635, architecture `volcano`)
- **Reference Device:** Fairphone 6 (`FP6`, `lineage-24.0`), which shares the SM7635 platform.

## 2. Hardware Subsystems & Fixes

### SurfaceFlinger & Display
- **Cpusets:** SF main threads pinned to cores `4-7` (mid/prime cores) to prevent dropped present frames during blur workloads.
- **HWC Strategy:** Keep `predict_hwc_composition_strategy=1` (verified to succeed 100% in hardware composer).
- **DPPS:** Set `enable_dpps_dynamic_fps=1` (aligned with FP6).

### Vibrator HAL (`hardware/nothing`)
- **Driver:** `rt6010` richtap driver.
- **Resonant Frequency (`f0`) Recalibration Bug:**
  - Sending `RICHTAP_SET_FREQ` on every `on()`, `perform()`, or `compose()` causes `unknown cmd` `KERN_ERR` in kernel logs because rt6010 does not implement runtime frequency reassignment.
  - **Fix:** Seed `f0` once during HAL initialization; update only on legitimate SFDC callback.
- **Thread Safety:** Cancel in-flight `compose()` worker threads whenever `on()` or `perform()` is invoked.

### Audio & Bluetooth
- **LHDCv5 Guard:** Ensure `persist.vendor.bt.a2dp.lhdc_v5` property is guarded properly to prevent Bluetooth A2DP audio dropouts after disconnect/reconnect.
- **Policy Cleanup:** Remove duplicate `audio_effects.conf` and dead A2DP/USB policy XMLs not loaded by the audio HAL.

### Camera & Sensors
- **OIS Calibration Symlink:**
  - Node `/data/vendor/camera/ois_gyro_offset` is created DAC 0600 system.
  - Camera HAL runs as unprivileged user and lacks read permissions + SELinux grants to `vendor_persist_sensors_file`.
  - Fix requires appropriate SELinux grant or copying during vendor_init with proper group access.

### Kernel & Security Subsystems
- **Branches:** `seventeen-ksun-susfs` (combining KernelSU-Next and SUSFS).
- **Security Audit:**
  - Removed `PRODUCT_REQUIRES_INSECURE_EXECMEM_FOR_SWIFTSHADER` which compromised `neverallow system_server execmem`.
  - Restored clean SELinux policies without permissive hacks.

# Sandboxed Google Play (GmsCompat) vs PixelPropsUtils

## 1. Architectural Conflict & Resolution
In Android ROM development:
- **PixelPropsUtils** spoofs `Build` fields (fingerprint, model, device, brand) specifically targeting Google Play Services (`com.google.android.gms`, `com.google.android.gms.unstable`) and Google Play Store (`com.android.vending`) to pass Basic/Device Play Integrity.
- **Sandboxed Google Play (GrapheneOS `gmscompat`)** runs official, unmodified Google Play binaries as standard unprivileged sandboxed applications with compatibility shims directly on top of the real hardware.

Running both spoofing and sandboxed Google Play within the same process creates severe instability and incoherent attestation.

### The Resolution Guard
In `frameworks/base`, `PixelPropsUtils` must yield whenever sandboxed Google Play is active:
```java
public static void setProps(String packageName) {
    if (GmsCompat.isEnabled()) {
        return;
    }
    // Standard spoofing logic follows...
}
```

## 2. Branch Layout
- **`seventeen-sandbox`:** Maintained across ~22 repositories (including `frameworks/base`, `packages/apps/Settings`, `manifest`) specifically for sandboxed Google Play integration.
- **`seventeen-oneui` / `seventeen-dualshade`:** Do NOT merge `gmscompat` into non-sandbox branches.
- **LineageOS forks:** Do not include either subsystem; maintain clean upstream lineage baseline.

## 3. Play Integrity, Attestation & Sepolicy Hygiene
When tuning ROM for banking apps and Play Integrity:
- **Sepolicy Cleanliness:** Never leave permissive domains or unlabelled node access in production policy.
- **Root & Debug Detections:** Remove all test-keys / userdebug traces visible to apps:
  - `ro.build.tags=release-keys`
  - Clean build dates and fingerprints matching valid certified targets.
  - No leftover su/daemons, ksu artifacts, or insecure execmem permissions.
- **Attestation:** Ensure Keystore keymint / boot attestation paths are untampered or cleanly shiffed.

## 2. Fast Patching Workflow (No Big Git Fetches)
Fetching entire histories of huge repositories (like `frameworks_base`, which is several gigabytes) exhausts device storage and bandwidth on mobile/Termux environments.

### The GitHub API Patch Pattern
1. Inspect commit SHAs using the GitHub API:
   ```bash
   gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits?per_page=10
   ```
2. Download individual patches directly without cloning full git history:
   ```bash
   curl -s -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.patch" \
     https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha> > /tmp/patch.patch
   ```
3. Apply patch index-only or with 3-way fallback:
   ```bash
   git apply --check /tmp/patch.patch
   git apply --3way /tmp/patch.patch
   ```

### Verification Without Builds
Because the user does not run repeated test builds:
- Inspect imports, method signatures, and symbol definitions in the target branch before applying.
- Check for missing proprietary dependencies (e.g., QTI BoostFramework or vendor services not present in the ROM tree).
- Never merge changes that introduce unreferenced classes or unresolved symbols.

# UI/UX, SystemUI & Launcher3 Architecture

## 1. Quick Settings (QS) & Media Customization
- **Brightness & Volume Sliders:**
  - Support high customizability: continuous resizing in portrait and landscape orientations.
  - Smooth corner radius scaling and interactive feedback.
  - Avoid heavy, bloated dependencies; use clean Jetpack Compose / Android UI primitives where supported by the target framework.
- **Media Player:**
  - Consistent padding and pitch across Quick Settings and notification shade.
  - Custom popup and compact states that scale properly with tile grids.

## 2. Dynamic Island / Live Activities Module
- **Design Goals:**
  - Lightweight, non-bloated implementation.
  - Dynamic states:
    1. **Compact Leading/Trailing:** Small pill state with icon and status indicator.
    2. **Expanded View:** Interactive overlay with media controls, timer, or notification actions.
    3. **Minimal Dual-Activity:** Split pill for concurrent ongoing activities.
  - Settings toggle: Allow users to enable/disable or configure layout and placement.
- **Display Cutout Safety on Nothing Phone (3a):**
  - Verify alignment against camera cutout and status bar margins.
  - Prevent left/right boundary clipping on corner radii.

## 3. Launcher3 & Launcher3Feed Integration
- **Glanceable Hub:**
  - Integrated via `GlanceOverlay`, `GlanceWidgetFrame`, `GlanceWidgetHostView`, and `GlanceWidgetPickerActivity`.
  - Dimensions in widget picker must strictly match the Hub layout dimensions to avoid resize glitches.
  - Resize handles must share visual styling and interaction semantics with system widgets.
- **Visuals & Performance:**
  - Dark-shaded opaque background styling for feed drawer and search surfaces.
  - Maintain steady 120Hz scrolling: eliminate frame deadline misses in launcher touch and swipe handlers.
  - Note: Live wallpaper FPS throttlers (e.g. Pixel MinimanWallpaper) may throttle independently; test jitter with static wallpapers first to isolate launcher performance.

## Open leads (RE, 2026-10-08)

- The QTI lights service (dropped 2026-10-08) ran `set_device_color`: it reads
  `/mnt/vendor/persist/color` ("Black" on this unit) and writes
  `/sys/class/leds/aw20036_led/dev_color` (labelled plain `sysfs`, reads `WHITE`). It also had an
  `allWhiteOn & rearCamOn` camera fill-light path. The OSS lights HAL does neither. After the
  next build, check Glyph colour/brightness and the camera fill light.
- `hal_fingerprint_default` reads an unlabelled property (`default_prop`, 5 denials). Label it
  in `property_contexts`.
- `hal_camera_default` searches `shell_data_file` (`/data/local/tmp`). Harmless; dontaudit if
  noisy.
